details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has voiced significant concerns regarding proposals to expand the market for euro-denominated stablecoins. During an EU finance ministers meeting in Nicosia on May 22, ECB President Christine Lagarde and other central bankers warned that broader adoption of euro stablecoins could pose substantial risks to financial stability and monetary policy transmission, potentially weakening bank funding and reducing lending activity. This stance underscores the ECB's preference for tokenized commercial bank deposits over privately issued stablecoins.
title: ECB Expresses Strong Skepticism on Expanding Euro Stablecoins

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) continues to highlight that tokenized finance, while offering efficiency benefits like faster settlements and increased transparency, carries risks of amplifying financial instability. A recent note from the IMF, discussed on May 26, 2026, emphasizes that moving financial services on-chain is a "structural shift" that could inadvertently remove frictions preventing financial crises from spiraling. The IMF stresses the urgent need for international coordination, clear policy frameworks, and robust governance to mitigate these risks, although it suggests "safe settlement assets" refer to wholesale central bank digital currencies, not Bitcoin or USDT.
title: IMF Warns Tokenized Finance Could Amplify Financial Instability

details: Bitcoin has experienced a turbulent period, with its price reacting to a confluence of macroeconomic factors including escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran, persistent inflation fears, and a "higher-for-longer" interest rate stance from the Federal Reserve. Despite strong institutional Bitcoin ETF inflows earlier in the month, recent weeks have seen renewed risk-off sentiment and significant ETF outflows, with one BlackRock ETF alone seeing substantial divestment from May 18-22. This has led to Bitcoin underperforming as traditional equities hit new highs.
title: Bitcoin Volatility Amid Geopolitical Tensions and ETF Outflows
